gaps.sentence: My usual barber's chair ___ (fix), so I'm trying a new salon.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + fixed for an unfinished, ongoing repair.

gaps.sentence: My laptop ___ (service) next week, so back up your files beforehand.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' takes the future passive: will be + serviced (is being serviced is also a valid arrangement).

gaps.sentence: The suspect ___ to have left the country.
The missing manuscripts ___ (find) — the search is officially over.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle. The result matters now.

gaps.sentence: The whole docklands area ___ (REDEVELOP) at present.
gaps.explanation: 'At present' signals an ongoing process: is being redeveloped.

gaps.sentence: Nothing ___ about the incident until the inquiry began.
gaps.explanation: Nothing was known by anybody: past simple passive was + known.

gaps.sentence: This bridge ___ repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Already' + present perfect passive: has been repaired.

gaps.sentence: All new students ___ (give) a locker key on their first day.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: are + given. Passives of give keep the indirect object as subject.
